extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians, mathematics educators, and the mathematical-sciences professional community (AMS members, institute organizers, grantmakers)
extracted.subtask_description: A collection of news and announcements for the mathematical community: prize awards, fellowship notices, institute program/workshop listings, calls for nominations, and commentary on editorial/administrative issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: d'Alembert Prize — scope and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Presented every two years, the prize recognizes outstanding books, articles, radio or television broadcasts, films, or other projects that promote public awareness of recent developments in mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prize amount for 1992 is 20,000FF; winners may be works in diverse media. Selection emphasizes effectiveness in promoting public awareness of recent mathematical developments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualities rewarded in a d'Alembert-winning book (example: Ivar Ekeland)
rubrics_metrics.description: "explains, in a clear, simple, and imaginative way, the great mathematical notions connected to chaos and their applications to physics and economics" and is characterized as "a dialetical fresco on order and disorder, determinism in indeterminism, and indeterminism in determinism."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The citation highlights clarity, simplicity, imagination, breadth (connecting mathematics to physics/economics), accessible exposition of topics (randomness, entropy, unpredictability, game theory, attractors, catastrophe theory), and humanistic/writerly qualities: 'not only one by a mathematician, but one by a humanist and a writer.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualities rewarded in a d'Alembert-winning outreach project (example: "Math en jeans")
rubrics_metrics.description: "Math en jeans" associates two secondary school mathematics classes with a research project under the guidance of a teacher and a mathematician; students (not necessarily top of class) devote two hours per week to topics like secret codes, non-Euclidean geometry, or the golden mean, define and explore questions, and present 'seminars' to allow fruitful exchanges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The project is described as a 'liberal and open approach' that creates opportunities for students who previously found mathematics 'cold and inaccessible.' The jury regarded this spirit as one of the best ways to bring a new vision of mathematics to young people.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alice T. Schafer Prize — selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The prize is given to an undergraduate woman in recognition of excellence in mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carries a $1000 stipend. Committee evaluation noted impressive achievements in coursework, independent study, competitions, and undergraduate research programs, as well as significant devotion to projects benefiting undergraduate mathematical life at their institutions; the committee also names runners-up and honorable mentions.

rubrics_metrics.name: MacArthur Fellowship — nomination and selection process
rubrics_metrics.description: MacArthur Fellowships are awarded with no strings attached and individuals cannot apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates are nominated by a group of one hundred designated nominators and awardees are chosen by a twelve-member selection committee which meets regularly. Fellowship amounts (in the cited year) range from $150,000 to $375,000 over five years depending on recipient age; funds may be used in any way.

rubrics_metrics.name: MAA Model Programs — selection criteria for case studies
rubrics_metrics.description: MAA seeks descriptions of highly successful undergraduate mathematical-sciences programs for dissemination to the mathematical community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically solicited are programs that: enhance recruitment and retention of mathematics majors; prepare a substantial number of students effectively for teaching school mathematics or for continued graduate study; or are particularly effective in attracting and addressing the needs of groups traditionally underrepresented in mathematics. Nominations (including self-nominations) are invited for possible inclusion in case studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed editorial criterion for Mathematical Reviews (MR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggestion that 'seminal' papers would receive in-depth special reviews selected by a special editorial body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such special reviews would be expected to include the historical context of the main results; implementing this would be a tricky issue (selection of which papers qualify as 'seminal') but is presented as a response to challenges in production/delivery and to make MR more useful and responsive.
